The core survives; four failure modes did not, and they apply to your proposal as written too. Folding them in now should make the owner ack a fast yes:

**1. Same-claimant concurrent claims race the state machine.** The claim tx reserves the *pool* row, but the *claimant* sandbox row's eligibility guards only flip at final transfer — so two concurrent claims for the same `userAgentId` (double-tap, client retry, two Worker replicas) can both pass reservation, mint on the same canonical key name (`createForAgent` is revoke-then-mint, so R2's mint **hard-deletes R1's freshly-applied key**), and interleave into a returned-but-dead claim + a double-claimed container. Fix: the claim transaction must CAS-reserve **both** rows (pool row state + a `claim_nonce`/state marker on the claimant row); the second request fails reservation → cold path. Your `identity_rotation_state` column is the right home — it just needs to live on/lock the claimant side too.

**2. Verify must probe the *resolved* credential, not the delivered one.** If the container-side apply endpoint verifies by using the key from the request body, it proves the key is valid at the gateway (already known) — not that the *running process* will resolve it for subsequent calls. Settings-precedence shadowing (boot env-fold over later writes — `runtime-composition.ts:66-97` is the in-repo precedent for exactly this hazard) can make apply "succeed" while the process keeps signing with the old identity. Fix: after applying, the endpoint must re-resolve through the same path the cloud plugin's client uses (`getSetting`/`resolveSetting`), assert fingerprint(resolved)==fingerprint(supplied), and run the auth probe with the **resolved** value. Acceptance should also assert one real *billed* inference row post-claim, not just an auth probe.

**3. The reconciler must be CAS-first, or it bricks slow-but-successful claims.** A rotation that runs long (retries near the deadline) can have the reconciler read `pending_*`, then the claim commits verified, then the reconciler proceeds on stale state — revoking the claimant key / quarantining a container that was just successfully returned. Fix: reconciler CAS-flips the state (`pending_*` → `reconciling`) and only acts on CAS-win; after a successful commit the CAS misses and it stands down. Plus a hard rotation deadline well under the reconciler threshold so overlap can't happen legally.

**4. Two failure-path ordering traps.** (a) Post-verify revocation-cache invalidation is fail-closed (throwing) in this codebase (#13417) — if it sits inside the same try as the claim finalize, a post-commit invalidation failure triggers the *failure* path against a *committed* claim (cleanup revokes the claimant's live key → acceptance #3 inverted by our own rollback). It needs its own post-commit try/catch that alerts but still returns the claim (your inactive-sentinel backstop bounds the exposure). (b) On apply-succeeded-but-verify-failed, the *claimant* key revoke must use the fail-closed invalidation variant — the claimant org is ACTIVE, so a warm auth-cache entry otherwise keeps authorizing from the unowned container for up to the cache TTL.

Supporting your impact correction: we independently verified migration `0107` seeds the sentinel org **and** user `is_active=false` and that the auth cache only stores fully-authorized contexts — so sentinel exposure on normal metered routes is ~zero, not merely TTL-bounded. Caveat worth a one-time prod check: both seeds are `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so an older prod seed could differ; and the `validateApiKey`-only routes audit you listed stays load-bearing.

Happy to turn any slice of this into tests/code under your review once the mechanism is acked — no code from us until then.

4. Even wiring the existing method as-is would not fix a mutable-tag rollout. `decideRollout()` compares only `docker_image` strings, while `rolloutStatus()` drops the persisted `image_digest`. [Manager](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/6659f25cd20eea80e4ad4a8a61a1e541b21551df/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/containers/agent-warm-pool.ts#L108-L124) [Status mapping](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/6659f25cd20eea80e4ad4a8a61a1e541b21551df/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/containers/agent-warm-pool.ts#L437-L451)
5. Pool capacity and claim eligibility likewise match only `docker_image`. Thus a ready row created from an older digest of the same `:develop`/`:stable` tag still counts as desired capacity and can be claimed. [Canonical claim predicate](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/6659f25cd20eea80e4ad4a8a61a1e541b21551df/packages/cloud/shared/src/db/repositories/agent-sandboxes.ts#L181-L208) The old digest is then copied onto the user row. [Claim transfer](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/6659f25cd20eea80e4ad4a8a61a1e541b21551df/packages/cloud/shared/src/db/repositories/agent-sandboxes.ts#L1738-L1748)

### User-visible consequence

After a tag's registry digest moves, a new dedicated user can receive an already-ready container on the old digest. Only after the warm-claim credential handoff reaches `running/ready` does that row become eligible for the ordinary digest reconciler on a later worker cycle, subject to the shared three-upgrade limit. This creates an avoidable old-image first-serve followed by immediate blue/green churn. If the configured image *reference* changes instead, old-reference rows become unclaimable but are also outside the image-filtered drain/replenish snapshot, so a healthy stale floor can persist until an explicit rollout.

### Acceptance delta for #16961

- Add a bounded daemon-owned pool image-rollout phase after successful pre-pull and before replenish.
- Resolve the configured reference to an immutable target digest and classify ready/in-flight pool generations by persisted `image_digest`; comparing tags is insufficient.
- Fence removal against the exact pool generation/claim race, preserve usable pool depth while replacing, and expose target/stale/replaced/failed counts.
- Make claim eligibility incapable of transferring a digest already known stale by the daemon; a subsequent user-fleet upgrade is not equivalent to a current warm claim.
- Make rollout status digest-aware instead of dropping `image_digest` or treating every mutable tag as unverifiable.
- Add contracts for same tag/different digest, same digest no-op, null digest, claim-vs-rollout concurrency, partial destroy failure/retry, and the real one-shot daemon phase/order. The existing decision tests cover different tag strings only, and the daemon one-shot test has no `rollout` collaborator/assertion.
